guard: a recursive delete refuses any target that is not a strict child of the root it was minted under, and a control socket path over sun_path is refused by name rather than by a bare EINVAL
why: THE GUARD IS GRADED THROUGH THE ASSERTION, NOT THROUGH A DELETE, and that is deliberate rather
than timid. The incident this file exists for was a cleanup that deleted the PARENT of its own
mkdtemp — on a host where tmpdir() is /tmp, that took an orchestrator's relay socket and
fourteen seats' control sockets, and stopped only on a root-owned EPERM. A fixture that proved
the fix by performing the delete would reproduce the outage to demonstrate that the outage is
fixed. The containment DECISION lives in assertContainedIn, so every mutation below disarms a
real branch of the real guard and every cell reads a refusal that did not happen — with no
traversing path ever reaching rmSync.
NO MUTATION HERE TOUCHES A PATH ANY SUITE LATER DELETES, MOVES OR WRITES INTO. The mutants
change comparison logic only; none changes what a path RESOLVES to, which is the class that
caused the incident and must not be re-triggered to test the fix for it.
THE THIRD MUTATION IS THE ONE THAT LOOKS HARMLESS. Swapping physical() for resolve() leaves a
containment check that still refuses '..' and still refuses the root itself, so two of the three
Part A cells stay green. Only the symlink cell moves. A lexical prefix compare is satisfied by a
symlink pointing anywhere, so that single cell is the whole difference between 'contained' and
'contained unless someone made a link', and without it the canonicalization could be dropped in a
tidying commit with every other cell still green.
PART B IS GRADED ON THE MESSAGE, NOT ON THE THROW. EINVAL already fails; what was missing was a
failure that names the path, its length and the limit. The cell asserts all three, so a refusal
that regressed to a bare throw would redden it.

mutations.name: the outside-the-root check is disarmed, so a target that resolves outside its root is deleted
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: a target that resolves outside its root is refused
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: a target that resolves outside its root is refused

mutations.name: containment stops being STRICT, so the root itself is accepted as contained
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: a target that resolves to the root itself is refused, not treated as contained
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: a target that resolves to the root itself is refused, not treated as contained

mutations.name: the target's existing components stop being resolved physically, so a symlink out of the root passes a lexical compare
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: a symlink inside the root whose target is outside it is refused
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: a symlink inside the root whose target is outside it is refused

mutations.name: the sun_path length check is disarmed, so an over-long socket path is returned for the bind to reject with EINVAL
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: a control socket path over the sun_path limit is refused with its path, length and limit
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: a control socket path over the sun_path limit is refused with its path, length and limit

mutations.name: the delete guard goes back to physical(), whose ENOENT fallback is lexical, so a MISSING target under a symlinked parent is certified by its spelling
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: a MISSING target under a symlinked parent is refused, not certified by its spelling
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: a MISSING target under a symlinked parent is refused, not certified by its spelling

mutations.name: the deepest-ancestor walk stops failing closed on a non-ENOENT errno, downgrading an unprovable target to its lexical spelling
mutations.find:
if ((e as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") throw e;
      // ENOENT FROM realpath IS AMBIGUOUS
mutations.replace:
if (false) throw e;
      // ENOENT FROM realpath IS AMBIGUOUS
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: a target whose ancestry cannot be resolved at all is refused, not downgraded to its spelling
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: a target whose ancestry cannot be resolved at all is refused, not downgraded to its spelling

mutations.name: an ENOENT from realpath is taken as proof of absence again, so an existing DANGLING symlink is walked past as if it were a missing basename
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: a target under a DANGLING symlinked parent is refused, not read as a missing basename
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: a target under a DANGLING symlinked parent is refused, not read as a missing basename

mutations.name: a `..` is applied to the SPELLING instead of to the physical prefix, so one that follows a symlink walks back into the root it had already left
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: a `..` after a symlink is refused when the sibling it lands on EXISTS (the shape this PR regressed)
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: a `..` after a symlink is refused when the sibling it lands on EXISTS (the shape this PR regressed)

mutations.name: the positive control mints unguarded again, so a TMPDIR over the socket budget kills the suite with a raw stack instead of skipping by name
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: under a TMPDIR too long for the socket budget the suite still reports a result, skipping the control by name
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: under a TMPDIR too long for the socket budget the suite still reports a result, skipping the control by name

mutations.name: the fixture teardown leaves the finally, so a suite that skips or throws leaks the fixture it minted
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: a skipped control tears its fixture down, leaving nothing behind
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: a skipped control tears its fixture down, leaving nothing behind
